question: A current of 1 A is drawn by a filament of an electric bulb for 5 minutes. Then the amount of electric charge that flows through the circuit will be _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**300 C**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The amount of **electric charge** that flows through a circuit is calculated using the formula: **Q = I × t**, where **Q** is the charge, **I** is the current, and **t** is the time.
 
• Here, the **current (I)** is given as **1 A** (ampere).
 
• The **time (t)** is given as **5 minutes**. Since the standard unit of time in this formula is seconds, we need to convert minutes to seconds: **5 minutes = 5 × 60 = 300 seconds**.
 
• Using the formula: **Q = I × t = 1 A × 300 s = 300 C** (coulombs).
 
• Hence, the amount of electric charge that flows through the circuit is **300 C**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Current (I)**__

 __
 
• The **electric current** is the flow of electric charge in a circuit.
 
• It is measured in **amperes (A)**.
 
• One **ampere** is equal to one coulomb of charge passing through a point in a circuit per second.
 
 
 
• **Time (t)**__
 __
 
• The **time** in this context is the duration for which the current flows.
 
• It is measured in **seconds (s)** in the International System of Units (SI).
 
• When given in minutes, it should be converted to seconds for calculations involving electric charge and current.
 
 
 
• **Electric Charge (Q)**__
 
 
• The **electric charge** is the amount of electricity transported by a current.
 
• It is measured in **coulombs (C)**.
 
• One **coulomb** is equivalent to the charge transferred by a one-ampere current in one second.
